name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent on every pull request before any human review. It catches 80% of trivial issues—linting, test failures, docs gaps—freeing humans for meaningful work. The trade-off is slower feedback for developers who must wait for the bot to finish, but that’s a net win because humans waste less time on obvious mistakes.

name: Gauge
text: PR-Agent’s 80% catch rate is a red herring—it normalizes mediocrity by teaching teams to tolerate trivial issues instead of fixing root causes. A better alternative is to auto-apply *only* safe, mechanical fixes (e.g., formatting) and route the rest to humans with clear criteria for what warrants escalation. Settle it by measuring whether PR-Agent’s feedback actually reduces *later* rework or human review time—not just initial "catch" rates.
